newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS - Italy seeks rapid ERM return, Paris supports.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Italy seeks rapid ERM return, Paris supports.

text.p: Italy on Friday said it wanted "immediate, rapid" talks with its partners on the level at which the lira could rejoin Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) and won public French backing for an early return.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi told a joint news conference with French President Jacques Chirac that European Union talks on the level at which the lira might re-enter the system should open "as soon as possible".

"This has to be the subject of immediate, rapid, technical negotiations at a multilateral level," Prodi said in Naples, where he held a morning of talks with the French president. He gave no specific date for a return to the currency grid.
France in the past has blamed its industrial export woes on the weakness of the lira since its ERM exit, triggered in September 1992 by a currency crisis.

But Chirac, whose attacks earlier this week on the lira almost pushed Prodi to scrap their summit, went out of his way to hail efforts by Italy's 20-week-old centre-left government to clean up state finances.

Both leaders also praised each other's 1997 budgets, crucial to their hopes of joining Europe's planned single currency in 1999, thus burying this week's angry spat in which Chirac had also questioned Italy's fitness to become a vanguard member.

"The courageous policy of rigour adopted by the government is in line with the European spirit," Chirac declared, adding: "The subsequent rise in the value of the lira and fall in interest rates can only be appreciated."
Prodi said no discussion of the lira's precise ERM level had been held in Naples because it was not a bilateral matter.
French officials said Paris had confidence in the multilateral EU monetary committee which will negotiate terms.
"We must have the re-entry of the lira as quickly as possible at a parity which is sustainable, durable and fair," Finance Minister Jean Arthuis told reporters.

The lira lost up to 40 percent of its value after its ERM ejection, boosting Italian export competitiveness. It has rebounded some 20 percent since 1995 and was trading at around 994 to the German mark in the early afternoon on Friday.

Prodi has previously said he wants the Italian currency to rejoin the ERM by the end of the year but at above 1,000 to the mark in order not to hurt Italy's industrial competitiveness. French officials have called for the lira to appreciate further.

ERM re-entry would be a vital step on Italy's path to economic and monetary union (EMU). Countries that meet stringent economic terms in the 1997 financial year will be eligible to join from January 1, 1999.

"The two countries expressed extremely favourable views on each other's (budget) measures," Prodi said, a retreat from swipes he made this week about alleged "window dressing" in France's 1997 package to help it leap the EMU hurdles.

He said there had been full agreement with France on all issues at the summit, from the Middle East and Bosnia to world trade, the war on drugs and the need to keep to schedule in an EU review of the bloc's workings which will be the subject of a special summit in Dublin on Saturday.
Journalists in the news conference room were able, by accident, to listen in on the plenary session of the talks via radio headsets designed to pick up simultaneous translation.
They heard Chirac say "there were no difference of views whatsoever between Italy and France on all the major problems".
Chirac said the glitch proved there had been no discrepancy in the public and private tone of the summit. "You've heard for yourselves that...the language is one and the same," he said.
